item.title: When Direction Becomes a Choice: Superconductors That Refuse to Go Both Ways
item.description: Superconducting diode effect, in analogy to the nonreciprocal resistive charge transport in semiconducting diode, is a nonreciprocity of dissipationless supercurrent. Such an exotic phenomenon originates from intertwining between symmetry-constrained supercurrent tr...

item.title: A Simple Rotation Bridges the Magnetic Divide
item.description: A universal SU(2) rotation transforms collinear density functionals into noncollinear ones, bridging a decades-old divide in magnetic theory.

item.title: Twin Phases: A Phase Transition That Breaks No Symmetry
item.description: Twin phases are distinct quantum states that transform into each other without breaking any symmetry, only rearranging internal symmetry labels.

item.title: When Molecules Learn to Squeeze Their Spins
item.description: For the first time, researchers have squeezed molecular spins using polar calcium monofluoride in optical tweezers, enabling quantum correlations that surpass classical measurement limits.

item.title: Coherent Chemistry: Doubling the Phase of Matter Waves
item.description: When ultracold cesium atoms merge into molecules, the molecular matter wave maintains a precise phase twice that of the atoms, revealing coherent wave-based chemistry.

item.title: Cools Both Ways: A Quantum Junction at Carnot’s Edge
item.description: A superconductor-insulator-2DEG tunnel junction acts as a Carnot-edge heat engine and bidirectional refrigerator, routing heat on demand with near-unity efficiency.

item.title: Hunting for the Magnet That Splits Nothing
item.description: In the altermagnet RbMn₂Te₂O, spin-up and spin-down electrons are split by nearly two electronvolts, while the crystal itself casts no stray magnetic field.

item.title: Seeing Wave and Particle Together: A Quantum Microscope’s First Image
item.description: A quantum-light microscope images a single polariton’s self-interference fringes in MoS₂, directly visualizing wave-particle duality at the nanoscale for the first time.

item.title: The Magnetism That Learns to Dance on Forbidden Tiles
item.description: A quasicrystal's never-repeating tiling hosts altermagnetic spin order with exotic eightfold symmetry, merging magnetic and geometric impossibilities.

item.title: A Neural Network Stumbles Into Topological Order
item.description: An attention-based neural network spontaneously discovers topological order in a fractional Chern insulator, revealing nearly degenerate ground states and fractional quasiparticles without prior knowledge.

item.title: Unshackling Weyl Points: How Periodic Driving Breaks Nature’s Pairing Rule
item.description: Periodic driving of an optical Raman lattice creates unpaired Weyl points, enabling a tunable chiral magnetic effect in ultracold atoms.
